sentences.text:
The Manager, A.P.S.R.T.C., vs Smt Ch.Sandhya Sunder, on 12
March, 2025
 The Honourable Smt. Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 M.A.C.M.A.No.2970 Of 2012
Judgment:

entities.text: Manager, A.P.S.R.T.C., vs Smt Ch.Sandhya Sunder
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1. Aggrieved by the Award passed by the Court of I Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge-cum-XV Additional Chief Judge, Hyderabad, in O.P.No.501 of 2010, dated 15.06.2012, the respondents in the said O.P. preferred the present Appeal seeking to set-aside the order of the Trial Court.

entities.text: I Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge-cum-XV Additional Chief Judge, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties hereinafter be referred as they were arrayed before the Trial Court.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioners, who are the parents of the deceased-B.K.Pallavi filed a petition under Section 163-A read with Section 166 of M.V.Act, claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the death of their daughter in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 10.04.2007.

It is stated by the petitioners that on 10.04.2007 at about 8.15 p.m., when the deceased was going to her residence at Malkajgiri on motorcycle along with her cousin by name Saradhi and when they reached DIET, Neredmet, one RTC bus bearing No.AP-9Z-5932 of Ranigunj- II Depot,
which was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, came in opposite direction and dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.

As a result, the deceased along with MGP,J her cousin fell down and the said RTC bus ran over the deceased and she sustained grievous injuries on her head, stomach and other vital parts of the body and died on the spot.

4. Based on a complaint, Police of Neredmet Police Station registered a case in Crime No.139 of 2007 under Sections 304A and 337 IPC.
5.
It is stated by the petitioners that the deceased was studying B.Tech 2nd year in Aeronautical Engineering Branch in MLR Institute of Technology, Hyderabad.
Due to sudden demise of the deceased, the petitioners were put to severe mental agony and hardship which cannot be compensated through any means.

Hence, filed petition claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/-
against the respondents.
6. Respondent No.1/Manager of APSRTC, Ranigunj depot remained exparte.

7. Respondent No.2/Managing Director of APSRTC filed his counter denying the averments made in the claim petition including, age, income, occupation of the deceased and contended that the claim of compensation is excess and exorbitant and hence prayed to dismiss the claim against him.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Based on the pleadings made by both the parties, the learned Trial Court had framed the following issues for conducting trial:-
1.
Whether the pleaded accident had occurred due to the negligent driving of the driver of RTC Bus bearing No.AP-9Z-5932 of the respondents?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation against the respondents for the death of the deceased-Ch.B.K.Pallavi?

If so, at what rate?
3.
To what relief?
9. Before the Trial Court, on behalf of the petitioners, PWs 1 & 2 were examined and Exs.A1 to A20 were marked.
On behalf of Respondents/RTC no oral or documentary evidence was adduced.

10. The Trial Court, after considering the evidence available on record, had partly-allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation of Rs.11,00,000/- along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization payable by Respondent Nos.1 & 2 jointly and severally.

Aggrieved by the said finding, the present Appeal came to be filed by the respondents/RTC in the said O.P.
11.

Heard arguments submitted by Sri S.Manish, learned counsel representing on behalf of Sri R.Anurag, learned Standing Counsel for TSRTC and Sri Madhusudhan Reddy Bhureddy, MGP,J learned counsel for the respondents/claimants.
Perused the record.

12. The contentions of the learned Standing Counsel for the appellant/RTC as stated in the grounds of Appeal are that the learned Trial Court failed to consider contributory negligence on part of the rider of the motorcycle and erred in fixing the income of the deceased @ Rs.12,000/- per month though she was pursuing II year B.Tech course at the time of accident.
In fact, she is dependent on the petitioners and hence requested to set-aside the order of the learned Tribunal.

13. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants contended that the learned Trial Court after considering all the aspects, had awarded reasonable compensation and interference of this Court is unwarranted.
14.
Now the point that emerges for determination is, Whether the order passed by the learned Tribunal requires interference of this Court?
POINT:-

15. It is pertinent to state that though the claim petition has been filed under Sections 163A and 166 of M.V.Act, since the learned Tribunal framed issues under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, this Court is inclined to consider the case under MGP,J Section 166 of M.V.Act but not under Section 163A of M.V.Act for calculating compensation.

2 16.

entities.text: Manager, A.P.S.R.T.C., vs Smt Ch.Sandhya Sunder
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is pertinent to state that though the learned Standing Counsel for appellant/RTC has urged as many as 7 grounds in the Appeal, but he has mainly focused his attention on two aspects viz., fixing of income of the deceased on higher side i.e., @ Rs.12,000/- per month though the deceased was studying II year B.Tech at the time of accident and application of wrong multiplier by considering the mother's age of the deceased.
17. A perusal of Ex.A18-Identity Card issued by KMR Institute of Engineering & Technology shows that the deceased is pursuing II year B.Tech student.

Though the learned Tribunal relied upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case between B.Ramulamma and others Vs.Venkatesh Bus Union and another 1 and took the monthly income of the petitioner @ Rs.12,000/- per month, but it failed to consider the point mentioned in the aforesaid judgment that there shall be deduction of 10% per year for students studying II year or III year.

entities.text: B.Ramulamma and others Vs.Venkatesh Bus Union
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, as the petitioner is pursuing B.Tech 2nd year, 20% has to be deducted from his fixed monthly income and after deducting the same, the net monthly income comes to Rs.9,600/-.
2011 ACJ 1702 MGP,J
Since the deceased being bachelor, if 50% of her income is deducted towards personal expenses, then the total loss of income comes to Rs.57,600/-.
After applying relevant multiplier '18' for the deceased being 19 years old, then the total loss of dependency would come to Rs.10,36,800/-.

The petitioners were also awarded with a sum of Rs.5,000/- towards funeral charges and a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate which this Court finds the same to be reasonable and is not inclined to interfere with the same.

Hence, the total compensation to which the petitioners are entitled to comes to Rs.10,56,800/-
18.
In the result, the Appeal is partly-allowed by reducing the compensation amount arrived by the Trial Court from Rs.11,00,000/- to Rs.10,56,800/-.
Except the said finding, the findings rendered by the learned Tribunal with regard to rate of interest and liability shall remain same.
There shall be no order as to costs.
19. Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
